classification.classification_note: SEC-bench metadata labels this sample as CWE-416, but the staged vulnerable source and saved sanitizer trace show a signed-length truncation that becomes an out-of-bounds read in `mpz_init_set_str()`: UBSan first reports unsigned-offset overflow at `bigint.c:665`, then ASan records a crashing read from an invalid address at the same line.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in mruby-bigint: mpz_init_set_str (mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c), invoked via mrb_bint_new_str, can read from freed or otherwise invalid heap memory when initializing a BigInt from a string. This results in a crash (SEGV) and potential memory corruption, with possible denial-of-service or further exploitation.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description, exact staged vulnerable source, patch.diff, sanitizer_trace.txt, and reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The saved PoC is plain mruby source, not a rite binary. `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt()` therefore routes it into the text parser, where `yylex()` materializes a decimal integer token whose exact digit string is 128 bytes long: `33333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333332770`. During code generation, `readint()` cannot fit that literal in `mrb_int`, so `new_litbn()` stores it as an `IREP_TT_BIGINT` pool entry and writes the token length into `buf[0]` as `char`. On this reproduced build, `(char)128` becomes byte `0x80`, so when the VM later executes `regs[a] = mrb_bint_new_str(mrb, s+2, (mrb_int)s[0], (mrb_int)s[1]);`, the stored length is sign-extended to `len == -128` while the base remains `10`. `mpz_init_set_str()` then uses `size_t i` with the loop header `for (i = len-1;; i--)`, so the negative length wraps to a huge unsigned start index and there is no `i >= 0` termination check before the first dereference. The first `s[i]` access at line 665 therefore walks before the digit buffer, matching the saved UBSan unsigned-offset-overflow report and the ASan crashing read at `mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c:665`. The staged fix repairs the same obligation by changing `i` to `int` and adding `i >= 0` to the loop condition.

source.description: First project statement that turns attacker-controlled source text into vulnerability-relevant state: the parser materializes the 128-digit decimal token as a `NODE_INT` carrying the exact digit string and base 10.
source.value_from: The saved PoC at `gt_results/secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42513165/poc` has sha256 `89e6013b788c8488a23112a290527b38a87f82f6cfbd23f8d27f904c6ff7be53` and contains one decimal run of exact length 128: `33333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333332770`. That exact token is what `tok(p)` passes into `new_int()` here.

sink.description: Crash sink. The bigint parser dereferences the digit string with a wrapped unsigned index that already points before the start of the 128-byte literal.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace first reports `runtime error: addition of unsigned offset ... overflowed` at `bigint.c:665:9`, then ASan reports `SEGV on unknown address ... The signal is caused by a READ memory access` in the same statement.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `mpz_init_set_str()` drives a descending digit loop from signed `len` using unsigned `size_t i` and no `i >= 0` bound, so a negative `len` is converted into an enormous index before the first read.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing `i` from `size_t` to `int` at line 646 and by changing the loop header to `for (i = len-1; i>=0; i--)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Stage 01 reproduced the bug by invoking `bin/mruby /gt/poc`; the CLI passes the attacker-controlled source file handle into the loader, which then routes the file into the text parser path.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC is admitted as plain mruby source rather than a rite binary because the initial bytes do not match the rite header and the early buffer contains no NUL terminator, so control takes the text-parser branch.

fine_trace.note: Source. While lexing the admitted source file, `yylex()` converts the exact 128-digit decimal run from the PoC into a `NODE_INT` token. The digit string and base 10 created here are the later inputs to bigint literal code generation.
The exact 128-digit token overflows `mrb_int`, so `overflow` becomes true and code generation chooses the bigint-literal path instead of emitting an immediate integer.

For this token `plen == 128`. `new_litbn()` stores that length in the bigint pool header as a plain `char`, so the first byte becomes `0x80` on the reproduced build while `buf+2` still points at the 128 copied digits.

When the `IREP_TT_BIGINT` constant is executed, the VM reloads the pool record and casts its header bytes back to `mrb_int`. The stored length byte `0x80` is sign-extended here to `len == -128`, while `s+2` remains the start of the copied decimal digit string and `s[1]` yields base `10`.
`mrb_bint_new_str()` forwards the digit pointer together with the sign-extended negative length into `mpz_init_set_str()` without validating that `len` is non-negative.

Root-cause step. In this vulnerable source `i` is declared as `size_t` at line 646, so the incoming `len == -128` is converted to a huge unsigned value at loop initialization. The loop also has no `i >= 0` stop condition or earlier `len` sanity check, so execution reaches the body with that wrapped index.

Sink. The first loop-body dereference uses the wrapped unsigned `i` from step 6 against the 128-byte digit buffer at `s`. UBSan reports unsigned-offset overflow on this expression, and ASan then records the crashing invalid READ at the same line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the root cause because it changes both the loop index type and the loop termination condition in `mpz_init_set_str()`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.

format.name: Plain mruby source with one exact 128-digit decimal literal
format.contract: A plain mruby source file that reaches bigint literal code generation with the exact 128-digit decimal token `33333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333332770`. In the vulnerable build, this exact length makes `new_litbn()` store `buf[0] == (char)128 == 0x80`; `mrb_vm_exec()` then sign-extends that byte to `len == -128`, and `mpz_init_set_str()` immediately dereferences `s[i]` with a wrapped unsigned index. The saved PoC at `gt_results/secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42513165/poc` is one such witness.
